Abstract

Let KKK be a finite extension of Qp\mathbb Q_pQp​ and let XXX be a good, Hausdorff, boundaryless, quasi-smooth KKK-analytic space. We prove that every locally bounded classically plurisubharmonic function on XXX is locally a decreasing limit of semipositive rational piecewise-linear functions defined over KKK on one fixed neighborhood. We use this regularization to construct mixed currents in the original Chambert–Loir–Ducros calculus. The unweighted currents are symmetric, closed and strongly positive. Their coefficient measures are Radon measures on the analytic space, so multiplication by a locally bounded classical weight uses its given Borel representative. These weighted products are jointly continuous along decreasing sequences with locally bounded limits, and the construction is compatible with étale pullback of the potentials. The regularization proof uses curve slicing, projective contact rigidity, and continuity of ample envelopes on normal models. A fixed vertical correction for mixed-characteristic test ideals provides the envelope estimate.

Introduction

Let KKK be a finite extension of Qp\mathbb Q_pQp​. A classically plurisubharmonic function on a Berkovich KKK-analytic space is an upper-semicontinuous function whose pullback to every analytic curve, after any complete extension of KKK, is subharmonic [10]. This definition tests positivity on curves and does not require the function to have a smooth local expression. The question addressed here is whether locally bounded functions in this class admit decreasing piecewise-linear approximation, and whether their curvatures have mixed products in the Chambert–Loir–Ducros calculus.

For continuous semipositive potentials, uniform approximation provides the mixed products. A locally bounded classical potential may be discontinuous. The recursive construction then requires multiplication of a current by a Borel function, and its continuity requires a limit theorem in which both that function and the current vary. We prove these assertions for the original CLD test forms. The approximation takes place over KKK on a fixed neighborhood of each point; all weighted products use the given pointwise representatives.

Proof strategy and relation to earlier work

The proof has two parts. We first pass from the curve condition to local decreasing regularization. We then use this regularization to construct the mixed currents and prove their continuity. The first part uses only first-order currents and products of continuous metrics, so it does not presuppose the products in Theorem “Mixed currents”.

The continuous products come from uniform approximation by semipositive model metrics. Approximation by Fubini–Study metrics and by smooth semipositive metrics is supplied by [3, Corollary 7.6 and Theorems 7.8, 7.14], in the current calculus of [5]. To treat a discontinuous classical potential vvv, we slice a test presentation by algebraic curves. The curve condition applies over the completed residue fields of the slicing points, even when those fields are nondiscretely valued. Thuillier’s lisse approximation and Dirichlet energy [14, §§3.4–3.5] give a positive Laplacian on each curve. Integrating these Laplacians gives the first-order current D[v]D[v]D[v], its coefficient measures, and the Green formulas needed below. The lisse functions are auxiliary piecewise-affine potentials on skeleta; the tests remain original CLD forms. We use the skeleton integration formulas of [6] on their original unit-moment presentations.

The passage to regularization is made on a smooth projective geometrically integral variety over a field in the finite unit-Gauss tower class GK\mathcal G_KGK​ of Definition def:gauss-fields, with an ample line bundle LLL. The contact theorem states that a bounded classical metric rrr and a continuous model-semipositive metric ppp satisfy r≥p,∫(r−p)c1(L,p)n=0⟹r=pr\geq p,\qquad \int (r-p)c_1(L,p)^n=0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad r=pr≥p,∫(r−p)c1​(L,p)n=0⟹r=p pointwise. Its proof is an induction on dimension. The first-order Green estimate controls the gap r−pr-pr−p against smooth backgrounds. A generic hyperplane then identifies its limit against the continuous background and reduces the vanishing assertion to dimension n−1n-1n−1. The hyperplane is defined over a unit-Gauss completion, which is why the induction treats arbitrary data over all finite unit-Gauss towers at once.

To obtain the approximants, choose continuous metrics ρℓ↓r\rho_\ell\downarrow rρℓ​↓r and take their semipositive envelopes sℓ=PLρℓs_\ell=P_L\rho_\ellsℓ​=PL​ρℓ​. Continuity and orthogonality of these envelopes give ∫(ρℓ−sℓ)c1(L,sℓ)n=0.\int (\rho_\ell-s_\ell)c_1(L,s_\ell)^n=0.∫(ρℓ​−sℓ​)c1​(L,sℓ​)n=0. Apply contact to max⁡(r,sℓ)\max(r,s_\ell)max(r,sℓ​) and sℓs_\ellsℓ​. Their nonnegative gap is bounded by ρℓ−sℓ\rho_\ell-s_\ellρℓ​−sℓ​, so contact gives r≤sℓ≤ρℓr\leq s_\ell\leq\rho_\ellr≤sℓ​≤ρℓ​ and hence sℓ↓rs_\ell\downarrow rsℓ​↓r. The envelope theorem is proved in Section “Envelopes on a normal model” on a normal model. Its algebraic input is the corrected subadditivity inequality of Theorem “Global fixed correction”; the vertical correction is independent of the ideals and their exponents and therefore contributes an error tending to zero after normalization by degree. To return to a local potential, Lemma “A common collar for decreasing families” realizes it, up to a constant, as a metric weight on a smaller fixed neighborhood.

For the mixed-current construction, the induction is on exterior degree. Strong positivity supplies coefficient Radon measures on the analytic space, making u1Tk−1u_1T_{k-1}u1​Tk−1​ meaningful before we differentiate it. To prove weighted convergence, we use Wu’s top-degree theorem for decreasing piecewise-linear potentials [16, Theorem 4.2(4)]. A complementary test is reduced to products of curvatures of auxiliary quadratic potentials. In middle degrees, this reduction is only modulo the annihilator of decomposable squares. Strong positivity kills that term in the current pairing, and the corresponding coefficient measure remains zero after Borel multiplication. Thus the reduction applies to every original complementary test.

It remains to replace decreasing PL sequences by arbitrary decreasing classical potentials. We first place the whole family on one projective variety, using the common bounds supplied by its first terms and its limits. A compact diagonal argument then chooses decreasing PL approximants whose current pairings approach the required ones. Choosing the common local domain before the approximants resolves the domain dependence noted in [16, Remark 4.6] for this class of functions.

Section “First-order currents and energy”, Section “Contact rigidity and decreasing regularization” establish first-order positivity and regularization; Section “Coefficient measures and the mixed-current construction”, Section “Decreasing families of classical potentials” construct the products and prove decreasing continuity. Section “Ordinary localization and the main theorems” transports these results to ordinary analytic charts and glues the currents. Section “Compatibility for specified potential tuples” treats specified potential tuples under étale pullback, including the finite-degree formula. The curve arguments, normal-model envelope construction, and common local domain are proved in the appendices. The index of notation records the definitions and normalizations used throughout.

First-order currents and energy

We construct D[v]D[v]D[v] by integrating curve Laplacians in the directions of complementary test forms. The resulting coefficient measures allow us to form the quadratic energy expressions for bounded potentials. These first-order expressions supply the contact estimate in Theorem “Projective contact and regularization”; no higher product of discontinuous potentials is used at this stage.

Definition. Let GK\mathcal G_KGK​ be the finite unit-Gauss tower class of Lemma “Countability of the auxiliary fields”. The induction below is carried out simultaneously over every F∈GKF\in\mathcal G_KF∈GK​, for arbitrary data defined over FFF. The residue field of such an FFF need not be finite or perfect. Its valuation ring is nevertheless a complete excellent mixed-characteristic DVR, and its compact analytic domains used here are metrizable.

For a current of bidegree (1,1)(1,1)(1,1), the complementary degree is n−1n-1n−1. Every (n−1)(n-1)(n−1)-vector on a face of dimension at most nnn is decomposable. This is the linear-algebra fact that permits the following reduction to curve-slicing directions.

Lemma (One-curvature complementary spanning). Let r=n−1r=n-1r=n−1. On a finite original moment presentation, every symmetric compact (r,r)(r,r)(r,r)-test is, after finite localization, a signed sum

η=∑ℓaℓΩℓ,Ωℓ=⋀b=1rd′ℓℓb∧d′′ℓℓb,\eta=\sum_\ell a_\ell\Omega_\ell,\qquad \Omega_\ell=\bigwedge_{b=1}^{r}\mathrm d'\ell_{\ell b}\wedge\mathrm d''\ell_{\ell b},η=ℓ∑​aℓ​Ωℓ​,Ωℓ​=b=1⋀r​d′ℓℓb​∧d′′ℓℓb​,

where the aℓa_\ellaℓ​ are smooth compact scalars and each ℓℓb\ell_{\ell b}ℓℓb​ is a rational linear combination of logarithmic norms of units.

Proof. Let EEE be the ambient moment tangent space. The orthogonal complement of the span of decomposable squares in Sym⁡2(⋀rE∗)\operatorname{Sym}^2(\bigwedge^r E^*)Sym2(⋀rE∗) consists of quadratic forms vanishing on decomposable rrr-vectors. Every rrr-vector in a face tangent space of dimension at most r+1=nr+1=nr+1=n is decomposable. Polarization therefore makes this complement zero on every face. Rational decomposable squares span the remaining finite dimensional space. Choose a finite basis from them and apply a fixed linear splitting to the smooth coefficient matrix of η\etaη. The scalar coefficients remain smooth. Clear rational denominators and use a finite original smooth partition of unity. For n=1n=1n=1 the assertion is the scalar statement with empty wedge. ◻

Proposition (First-order measures and positivity). Let F∈GKF\in\mathcal G_KF∈GK​, let X/FX/FX/F be smooth algebraic of pure dimension nnn, and let vvv be locally bounded classical psh on an ordinary open U⊂XanU\subset X^{\mathrm{an}}U⊂Xan. Then D[v]D[v]D[v] is a closed positive original current of coefficient Radon type. In every algebraic-unit curve-slicing presentation it satisfies the Borel kernel identity of Theorem “The curve Laplacian kernel”.

Proof. By Lemma “Exact replacement of analytic units”, the finitely many analytic units in a localized test presentation may be replaced, with exactly the same norms, by algebraic units on a fixed smaller norm-box interior. After clearing denominators, each direction in (eq:first-order-span) is given by n−1n-1n−1 algebraic units. These units define a map p:W→Gmn−1p:W\to\mathbb G_m^{n-1}p:W→Gmn−1​. When this map is dominant, its fibers over the base skeleton are the curves on which we use the subharmonicity of vvv. Choose a nonnegative coordinate top form on the base equal to its constant volume form near the projected test support. If ppp is dominant, Theorem “The curve Laplacian kernel” shows that a↦⟨D[v],aΩℓ⟩a\mapsto\langle D[v],a\Omega_\ell\ranglea↦⟨D[v],aΩℓ​⟩ is a positive Radon measure on WWW. If ppp is not dominant, the pairing vanishes by tropical dimension. The signed spanning lemma gives order-zero bounds in every coefficient direction. Smooth scalar relations and common refinements follow from Radon uniqueness.

The slicing argument gives positivity in constant decomposable directions. To obtain positivity on every complementary test, we must also show that coefficient mass on a face has tangent indices on that face. Closedness supplies this tangency. Multiply the coefficient measures by a nonnegative compact smooth cutoff and push them to moment space. Write their symmetric matrix as MIJM_{IJ}MIJ​, and view each column as an rrr-vector measure FJF_JFJ​. Closedness of D[v]D[v]D[v] implies that its distributional boundary is a measure; localization adds only the derivative of the cutoff times the order-zero current. For an affine linear equation ℓ\ellℓ, choose ℓϵ=ℓθ(ℓ/ϵ)\ell_\epsilon=\ell\theta(\ell/\epsilon)ℓϵ​=ℓθ(ℓ/ϵ), where θ=1\theta=1θ=1 near zero and has compact support. This cutoff tends uniformly to zero, while its differential detects precisely the mass on {ℓ=0}\{\ell=0\}{ℓ=0}. Insert ℓϵ\ell_\epsilonℓϵ​ times a compact scalar and a constant (r−1)(r-1)(r−1)-covector into the boundary equation. Terms containing ℓϵ\ell_\epsilonℓϵ​ tend to zero. Its differential is bounded and converges pointwise to 1{ℓ=0} dℓ\mathbf1_{\{\ell=0\}}\,d\ell1{ℓ=0}​dℓ. Dominated convergence for the finite coefficient measures gives (ιdℓFJ)∣{ℓ=0}=0.(\iota_{d\ell}F_J)|_{\{\ell=0\}}=0.(ιdℓ​FJ​)∣{ℓ=0}​=0. The equations of the affine span of each face therefore make both indices tangent to that face. On its tangent space every rrr-vector is decomposable. Positivity on rational decomposable directions, followed by density, makes the coefficient matrix positive semidefinite there. It pairs nonnegatively with every positive original test. For n=1n=1n=1 positivity is the curve statement.

The coefficient identities are identities of Radon measures and therefore remain valid after multiplication by a bounded Borel scalar, as in Theorem “The curve Laplacian kernel”. ◻

Proof. We first check that the energy expressions are defined using the first-order measures already constructed. Locally translate the bounded classical summands to be nonnegative. Their squares are then classical by convex increasing composition on curves. Polarization expresses squares and products of their differences as finite linear combinations of such squares. Thus Proposition “First-order measures and positivity” defines the differentiated terms in (eq:gamma), and its coefficient measures permit multiplication by the bounded gaps.

The curve chain rule of Lemma “Bounded curve energy”, transported through Theorem “The curve Laplacian kernel”, makes the quadratic expression nonnegative on each positive decomposable background. A smooth regularized-FS curvature has a positive semidefinite ambient Hessian, and their product is strongly positive. With one dominating coefficient measure, positivity on countably many rational directions passes by continuity to its variable decomposable directions. Polarization proves (eq:energy-cs).

Stokes against the smooth closed Ω\OmegaΩ gives the first equality of (eq:energy-green). For the second, approximate p,qp,qp,q uniformly by smooth regularized-FS metrics, keeping Ω\OmegaΩ fixed. The localized variation estimate of Lemma “Localized variation and Green formula” supplies an integrable factor multiplying the uniform approximation error on the curve slices. A finite partition of unity and the kernel formula therefore give Green symmetry with the continuous bbb. The positive continuous measures c1(L,p)∧Ωc_1(L,p)\wedge\Omegac1​(L,p)∧Ω and c1(L,q)∧Ωc_1(L,q)\wedge\Omegac1​(L,q)∧Ω each have mass VVV. Their difference gives (eq:energy-bound). ◻

Remark (The energy current). The current Γ(g)\Gamma(g)Γ(g) need not be closed. The face-tangency argument above is applied only to D[v]D[v]D[v]. Energy positivity is used on the strongly positive smooth backgrounds of Proposition “Smooth-background energy”. Its construction uses only first-order currents, independently of the higher mixed products.

Contact rigidity and decreasing regularization

In this section X/FX/FX/F is smooth projective geometrically integral, F∈GKF\in\mathcal G_KF∈GK​, and LLL is ample. The continuous products used here are constructed from model-semipositive metrics. Uniform pure-FS approximation and smoothing are valid over these fields [3, Corollary 7.6 and Theorems 7.8, 7.14]. Their model measure is

c1(L1,ϕ1)⋯c1(Ln,ϕn)=∑BbBdeg⁡B(L1⋯Ln)δxBc_1(L_1,\phi_1)\cdots c_1(L_n,\phi_n) =\sum_B b_B\deg_B(\mathcal L_1\cdots\mathcal L_n)\delta_{x_B}c1​(L1​,ϕ1​)⋯c1​(Ln​,ϕn​)=B∑​bB​degB​(L1​⋯Ln​)δxB​​

on a common normal model, where bBb_BbB​ is the multiplicity of the special-fiber component BBB and all intersection degrees are taken over the residue field. This convention retains residual degrees and the prescribed absolute value.

Definition. For a continuous metric ρ\rhoρ on LLL, let PLρ=sup⁡{s:s continuous model-semipositive on L, s≤ρ},P_L\rho=\sup\{s:s\text{ continuous model-semipositive on }L,\ s\leq\rho\},PL​ρ=sup{s:s continuous model-semipositive on L, s≤ρ}, pointwise in a common local frame. Nef rational model minorants give the same envelope: approximate a continuous competitor uniformly and shift its approximants down by rational valuation constants. Continuity and orthogonality of this envelope are proved in Theorem “Continuity and orthogonality of ample envelopes”.

The next lemma replaces one Fubini–Study curvature by integration over a generic hyperplane. It is used as an identity of measures: we will integrate the bounded, possibly discontinuous gap r−pr-pr−p against it in the proof of contact rigidity.

Lemma (A single generic hyperplane). Suppose n≥2n\geq2n≥2. c1(q)∏i=1n−1c1(ai)=1m ι∗∏i=1n−1c1(ai∣H),\begin{aligned} c_1(q)\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}c_1(a_i) &=\frac1m\,\iota_*\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}c_1(a_i|_H), \end{aligned}c1​(q)i=1∏n−1​c1​(ai​)​=m1​ι∗​i=1∏n−1​c1​(ai​∣H​),​

deg⁡E((LE∣H)n−1)=mdeg⁡F(Ln).\begin{aligned} \deg_E((L_E|_H)^{n-1})&=m\deg_F(L^n). \end{aligned}degE​((LE​∣H​)n−1)​=mdegF​(Ln).​

The first equality is an equality of Radon measures.

Proof. The associated morphism X→PFNX\to\mathbb P_F^NX→PFN​ is finite onto its image: the pullback of O(1)\mathcal O(1)O(1) is ample, so a positive-dimensional proper fiber is impossible. Generic Bertini in characteristic zero gives smoothness and geometric irreducibility of the hyperplane pullback; for irreducibility see [12, Lemma 37.32.3]. Completion of the Gauss parameter field preserves these geometric properties.

First take all aia_iai​ to be nef rational model metrics, and choose a common normal projective model carrying them and the generated model line of qqq. Work over R[Z0,…,ZN](π)R[Z_0,\ldots,Z_N]_{(\pi)}R[Z0​,…,ZN​](π)​ and then its completion. For an irreducible special component BBB, the incidence in affine coefficient space is the kernel vector bundle of the generating evaluation map. Its projectivization is a projective bundle over BBB. If the image of BBB under the generated linear system is a point, the generic hyperplane misses it, and its intersection degree with that generated line is zero. Otherwise the incidence dominates the parameter space; its generic fiber is integral. It need not be geometrically integral.

The multiplicity of the induced component is the original vertical multiplicity bBb_BbB​. This can be read at its generic point, away from the singular loci of the model and of BBB: the hyperplane cuts a parameter on BBB, whereas the uniformizer has order bBb_BbB​. Such generic points avoid every fixed proper closed subset of BBB in the universal incidence. Normalization retains the associated residual degrees. The divisorial points of the hyperplane model restrict to xBx_BxB​, and the projection formula for their intersection degrees gives exactly the coefficient of δxB\delta_{x_B}δxB​​ in (eq:native-model-measure). The root presentation of mLmLmL supplies the factor 1/m1/m1/m. Completion preserves normality because it is a regular morphism.

This proves (eq:single-hyperplane) for model metrics. Uniform approximation passes it to the stated continuous metrics, on both sides as Radon measures. Finally the algebraic intersection number of H∼mLEH\sim mL_EH∼mLE​ gives (eq:hyperplane-degree). There is no finite-degree factor for the transcendental Gauss extension. ◻

On the two fixed measures in the left side, the functions rℓ−pr_\ell-prℓ​−p are uniformly bounded and converge pointwise to hhh, so bounded convergence applies. ◻

Proposition (Local algebraic regularization). Let F∈GKF\in\mathcal G_KF∈GK​, and let uuu be locally bounded classical psh on an ordinary open of a smooth geometrically integral algebraic FFF-variety. Near each point, uuu is the decreasing limit of rational semipositive PL functions over FFF on one fixed ordinary domain. The approximants may be taken in Wu’s algebraic tropically convex PL class on that domain.

Proof. Choose an affine algebraic neighborhood of the prescribed point. Compactify it projectively over FFF, and resolve the compactification while preserving the smooth affine open [2, Theorem 1.1]. The resulting variety is smooth projective and geometrically integral over FFF, and contains the ordinary open on which uuu is given. The projective theorem applies to a global metric, whereas uuu is given only locally. Apply Lemma “A common collar for decreasing families” to the single function uuu. On a smaller fixed neighborhood it realizes u+cu+cu+c as the exact weight of a bounded classical metric on an ample line; outside a larger neighborhood the metric is supplied by a fixed Fubini–Study barrier. Theorem “Projective contact and regularization” provides decreasing pure-FS metrics there. Restrict to the fixed frame and subtract the same constant ccc. The inactive floor of Lemma “One inactive floor” gives the stated finite algebraic tropically convex representations, including at zeros of individual sections. ◻

Coefficient measures and the mixed-current construction

We construct the products by induction using Tk=D(u1Tk−1)T_k=D(u_1T_{k-1})Tk​=D(u1​Tk−1​). Two points require attention: the Borel product u1Tk−1u_1T_{k-1}u1​Tk−1​ must be independent of a moment presentation, and top-degree PL convergence must determine the pairing with an arbitrary complementary test. The coefficient-measure lemma addresses the first point and supplies the linear-algebra reduction for the second.

Lemma (Coefficient measures of strongly positive currents). Every symmetric strongly positive original current is of coefficient Radon type. On a fixed finite moment presentation its coefficient variations are bounded by finitely many positive cutoff evaluations. Consequently these variations are locally uniformly bounded in a weakly convergent family of such currents.

Proof. Put r=n−kr=n-kr=n−k, and let EEE be the ambient moment tangent space. Identify symmetric (r,r)(r,r)(r,r)-forms with symmetric bilinear tensors using the usual Lagerberg sign. Choose a rational basis eIe_IeI​ of ⋀rE∗\bigwedge^rE^*⋀rE∗, and put σ=∑IeI⊗eI\sigma=\sum_Ie_I\otimes e_Iσ=∑I​eI​⊗eI​. For any constant symmetric tensor AAA, choose CAC_ACA​ so that CAσ±AC_A\sigma\pm ACA​σ±A are positive semidefinite, hence weakly positive. If ϕ\phiϕ is an arbitrary original smooth scalar supported where κ=1\kappa=1κ=1, strong positivity gives

∣⟨T,ϕA⟩∣≤CA∥ϕ∥∞⟨T,κσ⟩.|\langle T,\phi A\rangle| \leq C_A\|\phi\|_\infty\langle T,\kappa\sigma\rangle.∣⟨T,ϕA⟩∣≤CA​∥ϕ∥∞​⟨T,κσ⟩.

The estimate applies to every original smooth scalar ϕ\phiϕ, including those that do not factor through the chosen moment map: pass to a common refinement, where pullback preserves weak positivity. Riesz representation therefore gives coefficient measures on the analytic domain itself.

Let WrW_rWr​ be the span of squares of decomposable rrr-vectors in Sym⁡2(⋀rE)\operatorname{Sym}^2(\bigwedge^rE)Sym2(⋀rE), and let Ar=Wr⊥A_r=W_r^\perpAr​=Wr⊥​ in the dual symmetric tensor space. Both signs of a tensor in ArA_rAr​ are weakly positive. Hence TTT annihilates every smooth coefficient times such a tensor. Its coefficient measure is zero, and remains zero after multiplication by any bounded Borel function.

We use decomposable directions after passing to the quotient by ArA_rAr​. Choose finitely many rational decomposable squares and a fixed linear splitting in that quotient. Every symmetric test then has a decomposition

η=∑ℓaℓΩℓ+B,B(t)∈Ar,\eta=\sum_\ell a_\ell\Omega_\ell+B,\qquad B(t)\in A_r,η=ℓ∑​aℓ​Ωℓ​+B,B(t)∈Ar​,

where the aℓa_\ellaℓ​ are original smooth compact scalars and the Ωℓ\Omega_\ellΩℓ​ are constant rational decomposable forms. The annihilator term is killed by TTT and by every Borel multiple of TTT.

All form relations and changes of presentation can be checked after multiplying by every original smooth scalar. Uniqueness of Radon measures then proves those relations as measure identities. This also proves compatibility with Borel multiplication. Finally, in a weakly convergent family, the finitely many positive evaluations on κσ\kappa\sigmaκσ converge and are bounded. Equation (eq:coefficient-bound) gives the last assertion. ◻

Remark (The middle-degree annihilator). The term BBB in (eq:full-test-splitting) is necessary. For dim⁡E=4\dim E=4dimE=4 and r=2r=2r=2, the Plücker quadratic z12z34−z13z24+z14z23z_{12}z_{34}-z_{13}z_{24}+z_{14}z_{23}z12​z34​−z13​z24​+z14​z23​ vanishes on all decomposable bivectors. The decomposable-square span has dimension 202020, whereas the symmetric tensor space has dimension 212121. Strong positivity kills this annihilator in the current pairing; it does not remove it from the original form sheaf.

To apply a top-degree convergence theorem to a test in complementary degree rrr, we will fill its rrr directions with curvature factors. The following quadratic potentials realize exactly those factors and admit PL approximants on the same domain.

Lemma (Auxiliary quadratic potentials). After fixed finite localization, every decomposable direction in (eq:full-test-splitting) is a product Ω=∏a=1rDha,ha=12ℓa2,\Omega=\prod_{a=1}^{r}D h_a,\qquad h_a=\tfrac12\ell_a^2,Ω=a=1∏r​Dha​,ha​=21​ℓa2​, where the ℓa\ell_aℓa​ are rational linear combinations of logarithmic norms of algebraic units. On one fixed bounded interval containing the range of ℓa\ell_aℓa​, approximate t2/2t^2/2t2/2 uniformly by finite maxima of affine functions with rational slopes and constants in λQ\lambda\mathbb QλQ. Such maxima are dense: approximate finitely many supporting slopes and their intercepts, using the density of Q\mathbb QQ and of λQ\lambda\mathbb QλQ. Choose errors ϵm=λ4−m\epsilon_m=\lambda4^{-m}ϵm​=λ4−m and add 3ϵm3\epsilon_m3ϵm​. The same margin calculation as in Theorem “Projective contact and regularization” makes the sequence decreasing to t2/2t^2/2t2/2. The interval, units and analytic domain remain fixed. ◻

Proposition (Top-degree PL convergence and normalization). On an ordinary algebraic analytic open of dimension nnn over KKK, decreasing sequences of algebraic tropically convex PL functions pi,j↓pip_{i,j}\downarrow p_ipi,j​↓pi​, 0≤i≤n0\leq i\leq n0≤i≤n, with locally bounded limits satisfy

p0,j MA⁡PL(p1,j,…,pn,j)⟶p0 MA⁡PL(p1,…,pn)p_{0,j}\,\operatorname{MA}_{\rm PL}(p_{1,j},\ldots,p_{n,j}) \longrightarrow p_0\,\operatorname{MA}_{\rm PL}(p_1,\ldots,p_n)p0,j​MAPL​(p1,j​,…,pn,j​)⟶p0​MAPL​(p1​,…,pn​)

locally weakly as Radon measures. The continuous PL stages agree with the original CLD products normalized by (eq:native-model-measure).

In logarithmic coordinates t∗=t/λt_*=t/\lambdat∗​=t/λ, pullback of a top Lagerberg form satisfies

∫Xanj∗α=λ−n∫X∗anα.\int_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}j^*\alpha =\lambda^{-n}\int_{X_*^{\mathrm{an}}}\alpha.∫Xan​j∗α=λ−n∫X∗an​​α.

Also j∗D∗pi,∗=λ−1Dpij^*D_*p_{i,*}=\lambda^{-1}Dp_ij∗D∗​pi,∗​=λ−1Dpi​. The factors therefore cancel in the calibrated top product: j∗MA⁡∗(p1,∗,…,pn,∗)=MA⁡PL(p1,…,pn)j^*\operatorname{MA}_*(p_{1,*},\ldots,p_{n,*}) =\operatorname{MA}_{\rm PL}(p_1,\ldots,p_n)j∗MA∗​(p1,∗​,…,pn,∗​)=MAPL​(p1​,…,pn​) as transported measures. Equivalently, both sides assign the same structural degree to every model component in (eq:native-model-measure). Inserting the weight gives the factor λ−1\lambda^{-1}λ−1, since p0,∗∘j=p0/λp_{0,*}\circ j=p_0/\lambdap0,∗​∘j=p0​/λ; multiplication by λ\lambdaλ returns (eq:wu-weighted). Thus the formula holds for the prescribed absolute value and the given functions, with the model masses in (eq:native-model-measure).

The constructed PL functions satisfy the stated local hypothesis by Lemma “One inactive floor”, Lemma “Auxiliary quadratic potentials”. In particular rational valuation constants are encoded by constant algebraic coordinates, or become rational under the normalization above. All uses of (eq:wu-weighted) are on compact tests; no global integrability assertion on a noncompact open is needed. ◻

Proposition (Construction and decreasing PL convergence). On an ordinary open in the analytification of a smooth geometrically integral KKK-variety, the currents in Theorem “Mixed currents” exist. If each potential varies in a decreasing sequence of algebraic tropically convex PL functions on one fixed open, with locally bounded classical limit, then the weighted currents converge on every original complementary test.

Proof. We prove existence in degree kkk from weighted convergence in degree k−1k-1k−1, and then prove weighted PL convergence in degree kkk. This order is required by the recursion: differentiation of u1Tk−1u_1T_{k-1}u1​Tk−1​ uses the undifferentiated argument at the preceding degree. For k=0k=0k=0, T0=[1]T_0=[1]T0​=[1], and the weighted assertion is bounded convergence against each fixed original top-form measure.

Suppose the statement holds in degree k−1k-1k−1. The coefficient measures of Tk−1T_{k-1}Tk−1​ allow multiplication by u1u_1u1​. Distributional differentiation of this Borel product defines TkT_kTk​ by (eq:recursive-current). Choose decreasing rational pure-FS approximants to its potentials on one fixed open. By weighted convergence in degree k−1k-1k−1, the Borel products formed from these approximants converge to u1Tk−1u_1T_{k-1}u1​Tk−1​ on every original test. Applying distributional differentiation shows that their continuous mixed currents converge to the TkT_kTk​ just defined. Finite convex-maximum smoothing makes each approximating current strongly positive. The limit is strongly positive, and Lemma “Coefficient measures of strongly positive currents” supplies its coefficient measures. Permuting the continuous approximants proves symmetry. Closedness and multilinearity follow from the recursion and the continuous identities. The recursion also makes the candidate independent of the chosen approximants.

We still need weighted convergence in degree kkk; it does not follow by multiplying the unweighted current limit by a discontinuous function. Use (eq:full-test-splitting). Its annihilator term has zero coefficient measure, so both the current and its Borel multiple kill that term. It suffices to treat a test aΩa\OmegaaΩ, where Ω=Dh1⋯Dhr\Omega=Dh_1\cdots Dh_rΩ=Dh1​⋯Dhr​, r=n−kr=n-kr=n−k, and the hαh_\alphahα​ are as in Lemma “Auxiliary quadratic potentials”. First we prove the unweighted identity of Radon measures on the analytic domain

Tk(u1,…,uk)∧Ω=MA⁡PL(u1,…,uk,h1,…,hr).T_k(u_1,\ldots,u_k)\wedge\Omega =\operatorname{MA}_{\rm PL}(u_1,\ldots,u_k,h_1,\ldots,h_r).Tk​(u1​,…,uk​)∧Ω=MAPL​(u1​,…,uk​,h1​,…,hr​).

Let ui,j↓uiu_{i,j}\downarrow u_iui,j​↓ui​ be PL sequences and hα,l↓hαh_{\alpha,l}\downarrow h_\alphahα,l​↓hα​ their uniform PL approximants. Decreasing families of classical potentials

Each classical potential has a decreasing PL regularization, but independently regularizing the members of a decreasing family need not preserve their order. We use a compact diagonal argument to choose one approximant from each row. The choice must both preserve decrease and satisfy prescribed bounds on current pairings.

Lemma (A compact triangular diagonal). Let ZZZ be compact, and suppose, for finitely many iii, that bounded metrics Ri,j↓RiR_{i,j}\downarrow R_iRi,j​↓Ri​ on one identified line have continuous decreasing rows Pi,j,m↓Ri,jP_{i,j,m}\downarrow R_{i,j}Pi,j,m​↓Ri,j​. Let δj>0\delta_j>0δj​>0 decrease strictly to zero. Given arbitrary thresholds for mmm, one can choose mj≥jm_j\geq jmj​≥j beyond them so that Qi,j=Pi,j,mj+δjQ_{i,j}=P_{i,j,m_j}+\delta_jQi,j​=Pi,j,mj​​+δj​ decreases in jjj and converges pointwise to RiR_iRi​.

The sets on which it holds are increasing open sets in mmm. Compactness gives one index for all points and the finite set of indices iii.

To force the correct limit, compare the chosen term with the first jjj fixed rows by imposing the finite family of caps Pi,j,m+δj≤Pi,a,j+2δj,1≤a≤j.P_{i,j,m}+\delta_j\leq P_{i,a,j}+2\delta_j, \qquad 1\leq a\leq j.Pi,j,m​+δj​≤Pi,a,j​+2δj​,1≤a≤j. The limiting left side is at most Ri,a+δjR_{i,a}+\delta_jRi,a​+δj​, so the same strict-margin compactness argument permits all these caps. Include the prescribed thresholds and mj≥jm_j\geq jmj​≥j. The decreasing limit QiQ_iQi​ is at least RiR_iRi​. For fixed aaa, the cap gives Qi≤Ri,aQ_i\leq R_{i,a}Qi​≤Ri,a​ as j→∞j\to\inftyj→∞. Letting a→∞a\to\inftya→∞ gives Qi=RiQ_i=R_iQi​=Ri​ pointwise. ◻

Proposition (Convergence for decreasing classical potentials). The conclusion of Theorem “Joint decreasing continuity” holds on ordinary opens in the analytification of a smooth geometrically integral KKK-variety.

Proposition (Continuous compatibility and top degree). The constructed currents agree with the continuous CLD products on their common continuous domain. Their top-degree weighted convergence holds against continuous compact scalar tests.

Proof. For continuous limits, decreasing continuous PL regularization is uniform on compact subsets by Dini’s argument. Continuous CLD mixed convergence therefore identifies the products. Conversely the recursive formula and Proposition “Construction and decreasing PL convergence” determine the current uniquely from any decreasing PL regularization.

In top degree choose a nonnegative original smooth cutoff equal to one on the test support. Its evaluations on the positive measures Tn,jT_{n,j}Tn,j​ converge by Proposition “Convergence for decreasing classical potentials”, giving a common mass bound there. The weights have a common bound MMM on a slightly larger compact neighborhood, so ∣Sn,j∣≤MTn,j|S_{n,j}|\leq M T_{n,j}∣Sn,j​∣≤MTn,j​ there. Uniform approximation of a continuous compact scalar by original smooth scalars then extends convergence to that scalar. ◻

Ordinary localization and the main theorems

The preceding constructions were made on algebraic charts. We now transfer them to the analytic spaces of Convention conv:spaces. The ordinary neighborhood must be fixed before regularization, and a finite change in the constant field must retain the original integration calibration. Once these points are settled, the recursive formula identifies the locally constructed currents on overlaps.

Proposition (Transport to an ordinary analytic chart). Every point of XXX has one ordinary neighborhood on which Proposition “Local algebraic regularization”, Proposition “Construction and decreasing PL convergence”, Proposition “Convergence for decreasing classical potentials” apply with the original KKK-calibration. For a finite decreasing family of locally bounded classical functions, the neighborhood and the projective variety can be chosen independently of the sequence index.

Proof. By Lemma “Ordinary algebraic neighborhoods”, a sufficiently small ordinary neighborhood is an ordinary open of a smooth affine KKK-variety. Its integral components are disjoint; restrict to the component containing the point. Let LLL be its finite constant field as in Lemma “Finite constants and integration”. The same variety is smooth geometrically integral over the finite ppp-adic field LLL. Take its projective closure and resolve that closure while preserving the smooth affine open [2, Theorem 1.1]. This gives a smooth projective geometrically integral LLL-variety containing the original chart. The preceding theorems apply with LLL as the initial field and GL\mathcal G_LGL​ as its auxiliary tower class. All local weights are functions on the identical original analytic chart. The algebraic LLL-functions used in their PL expressions belong to its original KKK-coordinate ring. If πL\pi_LπL​ is a uniformizer of LLL, then −log⁡∣πL∣Q=λQ-\log|\pi_L|\mathbb Q=\lambda\mathbb Q−log∣πL​∣Q=λQ. Thus these are rational PL functions defined over KKK, and the classical and model-semipositive conditions are preserved. For the currents, multiply the LLL-calibration by the single factor [L:K][L:K][L:K] in (eq:finite-constant-calibration).

For a decreasing family ui,j↓uiu_{i,j}\downarrow u_iui,j​↓ui​, choose this chart and a slightly larger compact neighborhood first. The endpoint inequalities ui≤ui,j≤ui,1u_i\leq u_{i,j}\leq u_{i,1}ui​≤ui,j​≤ui,1​ give common two-sided bounds there for the finite family. The common collar of Lemma “A common collar for decreasing families” therefore fixes the projective variety, line, frame and local domain for all indices. The potentials themselves are not required to extend to the compactification. The analytic isomorphism transfers every original test presentation, so it also preserves the current identities on every original test form. ◻

Proof of Theorem “Local decreasing regularization”. The inclusion Cb(U)⊂Rb(U)\mathcal C_b(U)\subset\mathcal R_b(U)Cb​(U)⊂Rb​(U) follows from Proposition “Transport to an ordinary analytic chart”. Conversely, semipositive PL functions are classical by [10, Theorem 4.3]. This result is applied on the strict ordinary algebraic charts just constructed; rational tensor denominators can be cleared. The decreasing-limit property of classical subharmonic functions on curves, with the all-extension quantifier, makes the pointwise limit classical [10, Proposition 4.2]. That limit is upper semicontinuous as an infimum of continuous functions, and it is locally bounded by the definition of Rb\mathcal R_bRb​. This proves equality on every ordinary open.

Now let uju_juj​ decrease in either class with a locally bounded pointwise limit uuu. The equality just proved makes every uju_juj​ classical. Since {u<a}=⋃j{uj<a}\{u<a\}=\bigcup_j\{u_j<a\}{u<a}=⋃j​{uj​<a}, the limit is upper semicontinuous. The curve decreasing-limit property again makes uuu classical. Applying the regularization assertion to this function gives membership in Rb\mathcal R_bRb​ on one neighborhood at a time. No intersection of the separate approximation neighborhoods of the uju_juj​ is used. ◻

Lemma (Equality and Borel multiplication). If two coefficient Radon currents T,T′T,T'T,T′ agree on all original smooth compact tests on an ordinary open, then hT=hT′hT=hT'hT=hT′ for every locally bounded Borel function hhh.

Proof. For a fixed compact original test η\etaη, the scalar functionals a⟼⟨T,aη⟩,a⟼⟨T′,aη⟩a\longmapsto\langle T,a\eta\rangle,\qquad a\longmapsto\langle T',a\eta\ranglea⟼⟨T,aη⟩,a⟼⟨T′,aη⟩ agree on every original smooth scalar. Smooth scalar density on a compact neighborhood and uniqueness of Radon measures give μT,η=μT′,η\mu_{T,\eta}=\mu_{T',\eta}μT,η​=μT′,η​. Integrating the given function hhh against this equality proves the assertion. The coefficient relations and common refinements are measure identities by Lemma “Coefficient measures of strongly positive currents”; finite localization therefore removes the choice of presentation. ◻

Proof of Theorem “Mixed currents”, Theorem “Joint decreasing continuity”. Construct the currents on the ordinary charts of Proposition “Transport to an ordinary analytic chart”. At degree zero their normalization is the intrinsic integration current [1]K[1]_K[1]K​, by Lemma “Finite constants and integration”. Suppose the constructions agree in degree k−1k-1k−1 on an overlap. By Lemma “Equality and Borel multiplication”, multiplication by the same Borel function u1u_1u1​ agrees there. Applying DDD identifies the two degree-kkk currents in (eq:recursive-current). A second application of the lemma with u0u_0u0​ identifies the weighted currents. Thus the local currents glue uniquely.

Closedness, strong positivity, symmetry and additivity in the differentiated arguments are local properties, proved in Proposition “Construction and decreasing PL convergence”. Positive homogeneity follows from the same recursion and approximation. A constant in a differentiated argument contributes zero because the preceding current is closed. Linearity of Borel multiplication gives the identity for the undifferentiated argument in Remark “The undifferentiated argument”. The recurrence and the continuous compatibility of Proposition “Continuous compatibility and top degree” give independence of PL regularization.

For joint convergence, Theorem “Local decreasing regularization” first makes each bounded limit uiu_iui​ classical. Cover the compact support of a test by finitely many ordinary charts and split the test into compact summands by an original smooth partition of unity. The compact-support partition theorem [6, Corollary 15.2.9] is sufficient; no global paracompactness assumption is needed. On each slightly larger compact subchart the bounded endpoints give the common bounds used in Proposition “Convergence for decreasing classical potentials”. Apply that proposition, restore the single constant-field factor, and sum. Only the test forms are partitioned. Taking a constant weight proves the unweighted convergence. In top degree, the cutoff mass argument in Proposition “Continuous compatibility and top degree” extends convergence to all continuous compact scalar tests. ◻

Proof of Corollary cor:quasiprojective. The analytification of a smooth separated variety over KKK is good, Hausdorff, quasi-smooth and without relative analytic boundary [13, Exercise 5.1.1(iii), Fact 5.1.5]. These properties are preserved on ordinary opens. Every compact test uses only finitely many relatively compact charts inside the given open, to which the main theorems apply. ◻

Remark (Two different boundaries). If Y⊂Y‾Y\subset\overline YY⊂Y is a projective compactification, the deleted algebraic locus Y‾∖Y\overline Y\setminus YY∖Y differs from the relative analytic boundary of Yan→M(K)Y^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathcal M(K)Yan→M(K), which is empty for smooth YYY. A potential can be unbounded near the deleted algebraic locus and remain locally bounded at every point of YanY^{\mathrm{an}}Yan. The present theorems apply on that ordinary open and make no claim about extension of the potential to Y‾an\overline Y^{\mathrm{an}}Yan. For a singular variety they apply on its smooth locus.

Compatibility for specified potential tuples

For a specified tuple of potentials, composition with an étale map gives another tuple of locally bounded classical potentials. The next theorem identifies its mixed current with the limit of the continuous-stage pullbacks. Thus the operation is defined through the potentials and their decreasing regularizations; no pullback of an arbitrary distributional current is required.

Theorem (Étale compatibility). Let f:Y→Xf:Y\to Xf:Y→X be étale between spaces satisfying Convention conv:spaces. Let W⊂XW\subset XW⊂X be an ordinary open on which a finite tuple u0,…,uk∈Cb(W)u_0,\ldots,u_k\in\mathcal C_b(W)u0​,…,uk​∈Cb​(W) has decreasing continuous semipositive regularizations ai,m↓uia_{i,m}\downarrow u_iai,m​↓ui​. Then, on every original compact test in f−1(W)f^{-1}(W)f−1(W),

Sk,Y(a0,m∘f;a1,m∘f,…,ak,m∘f)⟶Sk,Y(u0∘f;u1∘f,…,uk∘f).S_{k,Y}(a_{0,m}\circ f;a_{1,m}\circ f,\ldots,a_{k,m}\circ f) \longrightarrow S_{k,Y}(u_0\circ f;u_1\circ f,\ldots,u_k\circ f).Sk,Y​(a0,m​∘f;a1,m​∘f,…,ak,m​∘f)⟶Sk,Y​(u0​∘f;u1​∘f,…,uk​∘f).

This extension of the continuous-stage operation is independent of the regularizations and commutes with ordinary restriction and composition of étale maps.

Proof. Composition of curve tests preserves classicality, and continuity of fff preserves local boundedness. At a continuous stage, local uniform smooth semipositive approximation and the pullback identity for smooth forms identify the pulled-back operation with the continuous mixed product of the pulled-back weights. To obtain the required smooth approximations, apply Theorem “Local decreasing regularization” to a continuous weight. Its decreasing PL approximation is uniform on a smaller compact neighborhood by Dini’s theorem. In the pure-FS presentations furnished by the proof, smoothing the convex maximum gives original smooth semipositive weights with the same uniform limit; see [3, Theorem 7.14]. The argument is local on both spaces. Theorem “Joint decreasing continuity” on YYY gives (eq:etale-tuple) with the Borel product on its right, for every choice of base regularization. For an étale map g:Z→Yg:Z\to Yg:Z→Y, pull the same continuous approximants twice and apply the theorem on ZZZ. Both operations give the weighted current of (ui∘f∘g)i(u_i\circ f\circ g)_i(ui​∘f∘g)i​. Restriction follows from locality. ◻

Proposition (The finite-étale degree formula). Let f:Y→Xf:Y\to Xf:Y→X be finite étale of constant degree ddd. For every tuple u0,…,uk∈Cb(X)u_0,\ldots,u_k\in\mathcal C_b(X)u0​,…,uk​∈Cb​(X),

f∗Sk,Y(u0∘f;u1∘f,…,uk∘f)=dSk,X(u0;u1,…,uk),\begin{aligned} f_*S_{k,Y}(u_0\circ f;u_1\circ f,\ldots,u_k\circ f) &=dS_{k,X}(u_0;u_1,\ldots,u_k),\end{aligned}f∗​Sk,Y​(u0​∘f;u1​∘f,…,uk​∘f)​=dSk,X​(u0​;u1​,…,uk​),​

f∗Tk,Y(u1∘f,…,uk∘f)=dTk,X(u1,…,uk).\begin{aligned} f_*T_{k,Y}(u_1\circ f,\ldots,u_k\circ f) &=dT_{k,X}(u_1,\ldots,u_k). \end{aligned}f∗​Tk,Y​(u1​∘f,…,uk​∘f)​=dTk,X​(u1​,…,uk​).​

Proposition (Descent of the bounded class). Let f:Y→Xf:Y\to Xf:Y→X be a finite étale surjection and uuu a given real function on XXX. If u∘f∈Cb(Y)u\circ f\in\mathcal C_b(Y)u∘f∈Cb​(Y), then u∈Cb(X)=Rb(X)u\in\mathcal C_b(X)=\mathcal R_b(X)u∈Cb​(X)=Rb​(X). Membership of a given function in this class is also local for étale covers.

Proof. Classical subharmonicity descends under the finite surjection by [10, Proposition 4.2(6)]. A finite surjection is proper and closed, so upper semicontinuity and local boundedness descend as follows. Since {u≥a}=f({u∘f≥a})\{u\geq a\}=f(\{u\circ f\geq a\}){u≥a}=f({u∘f≥a}), upper semicontinuity descends. Cover the finite fiber above xxx by finitely many open neighborhoods on which u∘fu\circ fu∘f is bounded, let VVV be their union, and choose a common bound MMM. The ordinary open X∖f(Y∖V)X\setminus f(Y\setminus V)X∖f(Y∖V) contains xxx, and its entire inverse image lies in VVV. Surjectivity gives ∣u∣≤M|u|\leq M∣u∣≤M there.

For an étale cover, choose a point above xxx and a local finite-étale representative on compact analytic neighborhoods [6, §11.6.3 and Lemma 11.6.5(a)]. Restrict the target to an ordinary open in its relative interior. The locally separated interior formula used in Lemma “Ordinary algebraic neighborhoods” makes its inverse image ordinary open in the source. The positive-degree component supplies a finite-étale surjection near xxx. The first assertion and ordinary locality apply. Finally Theorem “Local decreasing regularization” gives the local regularization on XXX. ◻

Remark (Descent data). Proposition “Descent of the bounded class” concerns a function already given on the base. Functions independently chosen on different sheets need not descend: constants 000 and 111 on two disjoint copies of a ball provide an example.

Curve Laplacians and Borel slicing

The slicing formula in this appendix expresses the first-order current of Proposition “First-order measures and positivity” as an integral of positive curve Laplacians. Its measure-theoretic form is needed when the test coefficient is only Borel. The measure identities in this section are identities on analytic spaces. In particular, a Borel coefficient is not replaced by a function on the image of a moment map. Put D=d′d′′D=\mathrm d'\mathrm d''D=d′d′′. On a smooth analytic curve we use the sign for which the Laplacian of a convex function on an oriented annulus has nonnegative second derivative. With weights −log⁡∥e∥-\log\|e\|−log∥e∥, this is the sign for which a semipositive model metric has positive curvature of mass equal to the degree of its line bundle. Original unit-moment forms are used throughout. The integration theory of [6, §15.1 and §15.3] restricts on these presentations to the original one: both integrate their Lagerberg representatives with the canonical finite-degree calibration. Thus the use below of the more general skeleton formulation in [6] changes neither the test forms nor their integrals; compare the original calibration in [5, §3.5].

Lemma (Countability of the auxiliary fields). Let K/QpK/\mathbb Q_pK/Qp​ be finite. Let GK\mathcal G_KGK​ consist of the fields obtained from KKK by finitely many operations E⟼E(Z1,…,Zs)^Gauss,∣Zi∣=1.E\longmapsto \widehat{E(Z_1,\ldots,Z_s)}_{\mathrm{Gauss}}, \qquad |Z_i|=1.E⟼E(Z1​,…,Zs​)​Gauss​,∣Zi​∣=1. Every F∈GKF\in\mathcal G_KF∈GK​ has a countable dense subfield. Its valuation ring is a complete excellent discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic, with the same value group as KKK. Every compact analytic domain admitting a finite affinoid cover in a good Hausdorff FFF-analytic space is metrizable. Locally in such a space, ordinary analytic opens admit countable compact exhaustions and countable families of original smooth scalar functions that are uniformly dense on each fixed compact support.

Proof. A Q\mathbb QQ-span of a Qp\mathbb Q_pQp​-basis of KKK is countable and dense; the subfield it generates is still countable. If E0⊂EE_0\subset EE0​⊂E is a countable dense subfield, then E0(Z1,…,Zs)E_0(Z_1,\ldots,Z_s)E0​(Z1​,…,Zs​) is dense for the unit Gauss valuation in E(Z1,…,Zs)E(Z_1,\ldots,Z_s)E(Z1​,…,Zs​) and hence in its completion. The valuation ring after one step is the completion of E∘[Z1,…,Zs](π)E^\circ[Z_1,\ldots,Z_s]_{(\pi)}E∘[Z1​,…,Zs​](π)​. This is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer π\piπ and residue field E~(Z1,…,Zs)\widetilde E(Z_1,\ldots,Z_s)E(Z1​,…,Zs​). Its completion is excellent.

An affinoid algebra over a field with a countable dense subfield has a countable dense subset. Evaluation of the absolute values of these elements embeds its Berkovich spectrum in a countable product of compact intervals: uniform approximation determines the value of every other element. The spectrum is therefore compact metrizable. A finite affinoid cover gives the assertion for compact domains. An ordinary open in such a compact neighborhood is locally compact and second countable, and admits a countable compact exhaustion. Original smooth partitions of unity and uniform smooth density [6, Theorem 15.2.6 and Corollary 15.2.7] give the last assertion. For a fixed compact set one first chooses a larger compact neighborhood and a smooth cutoff equal to one on the smaller set, and then takes a countable dense subset of the resulting separable space of continuous functions. ◻

Lemma (Compatibility of curve Laplacians). Let EEE be a complete nontrivially valued field of characteristic zero, and let CCC be an ordinary open in the analytification of a smooth algebraic EEE-curve. A locally bounded subharmonic function bbb has a positive Radon Laplacian ΔCb\Delta_C bΔC​b, and

∫Ca d(ΔCb)=∫Cb Da(a∈Ac0,0(C)).\int_C a\,d(\Delta_C b)=\int_C b\,Da \qquad(a\in A_c^{0,0}(C)).∫C​ad(ΔC​b)=∫C​bDa(a∈Ac0,0​(C)).

Both sides use the canonical calibration over EEE. The assertion does not require the residue field of EEE to be algebraic over a finite field.

Proof. The open CCC is strictly analytic. Thuillier’s Theorem 3.4.12 gives its positive Radon Laplacian, and Theorem 3.4.2 gives, on a relatively compact larger open, a decreasing net bνb_\nubν​ of lisse subharmonic functions with limit bbb [14]. Here lisse means piecewise affine on a finite semistable skeleton after a finite extension; it does not mean original CLD smooth. The relation between this subharmonicity and the curve convention used here is [10, §3.3.1–§3.3.2].

For a lisse function, (eq:curve-original-test) follows from integration by parts on a common finite skeleton for the function and the original moment presentation of aaa. Along an annular edge the formula is the one-variable integration-by-parts formula; the endpoint terms are the weighted outgoing slopes. These are precisely the atoms of the lisse Laplacian. The edge weights retain the residue degrees. A finite extension used to obtain the skeleton can be removed by the calibrated base-extension integration formula [6, §15.3, Proposition 14.3.6]; both sides have the same normalization. This is also the lisse comparison underlying [15, Proposition 4.2].

On a compact neighborhood of supp⁡a\operatorname{supp}asuppa, a tail of bνb_\nubν​ is bounded above, while bbb bounds it below. Integration of a decreasing net of continuous functions against a finite Radon measure commutes with its infimum. To see this, a continuous function strictly above the infimum eventually dominates the net on the compact set: the sets on which this domination holds form an increasing open cover. Compactness gives one index. Taking the infimum of the integrals of continuous majorants proves the assertion by Radon regularity. Apply this to the positive and negative parts of the fixed measure DaDaDa. The Laplacians converge as distributions by Thuillier’s construction; their masses on a smaller compact set are bounded by testing against one nonnegative lisse cutoff. Uniform density then permits every continuous compact test, including aaa. Passing to the limit gives (eq:curve-original-test). ◻

In the applications below, ppp is formed from the units in a decomposable complementary direction; a coordinate cutoff ω=1\omega=1ω=1 near the projected test support gives exactly the displayed class of base forms. When n=1n=1n=1, the base is a point and the statement is Lemma “Compatibility of curve Laplacians”. If ppp is not dominant, its top-degree base form pulls back to zero by tropical dimension, and the corresponding first-order pairing is zero.

Return to “First-order currents and energy” (first-order positivity).

Bounded curve energy and a localized Green estimate

The local estimate below transfers differentiation from a continuous potential to a compactly supported bounded weight. Its total variation bound then controls the error when the continuous potential varies uniformly, even though the weight may be discontinuous. It is used in Proposition “Smooth-background energy”; the proper-curve identity supplies the initial case of Theorem “Projective contact and regularization”.

We retain the curve convention of Lemma “Compatibility of curve Laplacians”. The field in this appendix is complete and nontrivially valued of characteristic zero. The curves used below are ordinary opens in smooth algebraic curves; in particular they are strictly analytic. The operator DDD on a lisse function is its weighted graph Laplacian. Original smooth functions on a common skeleton are piecewise smooth graph functions, and the same integration-by-parts formula applies to them.

Lemma (Bounded curve energy). Locally bounded subharmonic functions have locally finite Dirichlet energy. For a finite real linear combination bbb of such functions, the expression ΓC(b)=12D[b2]−bD[b]\Gamma_C(b)=\tfrac12D[b^2]-bD[b]ΓC​(b)=21​D[b2]−bD[b] is a nonnegative Radon measure. Its polarization is bilinear and satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz on compact supports. The product and chain rules are

D[ab]=aD[b]+bD[a]+2ΓC(a,b),\begin{aligned} D[ab]&=aD[b]+bD[a]+2\Gamma_C(a,b),\end{aligned}D[ab]​=aD[b]+bD[a]+2ΓC​(a,b),​

D[Φ(b)]=Φ′(b)D[b]+Φ′′(b)ΓC(b)\begin{aligned} D[\Phi(b)]&=\Phi'(b)D[b]+\Phi''(b)\Gamma_C(b) \end{aligned}D[Φ(b)]​=Φ′(b)D[b]+Φ′′(b)ΓC​(b)​

whenever the functions are locally bounded and Φ\PhiΦ is C2C^2C2 on a neighborhood of their relevant range.

On a smooth proper connected curve, if r,pr,pr,p are bounded subharmonic metrics on the same line, then their gap g=r−pg=r-pg=r−p satisfies

EC(g)=−∫gD[g]≥0.E_C(g)=-\int gD[g]\geq0.EC​(g)=−∫gD[g]≥0.

The associated Green pairing is symmetric. If EC(g)=0E_C(g)=0EC​(g)=0, the function ggg is constant pointwise.

Proof. We recall how boundedness puts these statements within the complete-field curve theory. On a compact domain inside a larger curve open, Thuillier’s harmonic interpolants give lisse subharmonic functions bS↓bb_S\downarrow bbS​↓b, indexed by finite sets of nonrigid points containing the boundary [14, Theorem 3.4.2]. Their values on each such set are the values of the given function bbb. At an additional fixed inner boundary these values can be kept fixed by including its finitely many points in every SSS.

Take original smooth cutoffs 0≤ρ,κ≤10\leq\rho,\kappa\leq10≤ρ,κ≤1, with κ=1\kappa=1κ=1 near supp⁡ρ\operatorname{supp}\rhosuppρ, on the larger domain. A tail of the interpolants is bounded by M+ϵM+\epsilonM+ϵ on these compact supports if ∣b∣≤M|b|\leq M∣b∣≤M; this follows from the increasing open cover {bS<M+ϵ}\{b_S<M+\epsilon\}{bS​<M+ϵ}. On a common finite skeleton, the graph product formula gives, with xS2=∫ρ2ΓC(bS)x_S^2=\int\rho^2\Gamma_C(b_S)xS2​=∫ρ2ΓC​(bS​),

xS2≤(M+ϵ)2∥Dκ∥TV+2(M+ϵ)xS(∫ΓC(ρ))1/2.x_S^2\leq (M+\epsilon)^2\|D\kappa\|_{\rm TV} +2(M+\epsilon)x_S \left(\int\Gamma_C(\rho)\right)^{1/2}.xS2​≤(M+ϵ)2∥Dκ∥TV​+2(M+ϵ)xS​(∫ΓC​(ρ))1/2.

Indeed ∫supp⁡ρDbS≤(M+ϵ)∥Dκ∥TV\int_{\operatorname{supp}\rho}Db_S\leq (M+\epsilon)\|D\kappa\|_{\rm TV}∫suppρ​DbS​≤(M+ϵ)∥Dκ∥TV​, by testing against κ\kappaκ, and integration by parts in ∫ρ2 d′bS d′′bS\int \rho^2\,d'b_S\,d''b_S∫ρ2d′bS​d′′bS​ gives the displayed mixed term. Thus the local Dirichlet energies are bounded.

Subtracting the fixed harmonic extension of the inner boundary values places the interpolants in the Dirichlet space with zero boundary values. The finite-skeleton harmonic interpolants are the orthogonal projections to the corresponding finite-dimensional Dirichlet subspaces. Their energies increase under refinement; the bound above puts their limit in the Hilbert completion. For nested point sets S⊂S′S\subset S'S⊂S′, orthogonality gives ∥bS′−bS∥D2=∥bS′∥D2−∥bS∥D2\|b_{S'}-b_S\|_D^2 =\|b_{S'}\|_D^2-\|b_S\|_D^2∥bS′​−bS​∥D2​=∥bS′​∥D2​−∥bS​∥D2​ after the fixed harmonic extension has been subtracted. The bounded increasing energies therefore make this net Cauchy. Its distributional limit is bbb, so its Dirichlet limit represents the same potential. This is the construction and projection argument in [14, §3.5, especially Lemma 3.5.3 and the discussion following it]. It applies simultaneously to a finite list of bounded subharmonic functions.

Products of bounded Dirichlet functions and C2C^2C2 compositions satisfy the graph product and chain rules. These rules pass from the interpolants to the Dirichlet limit: boundedness controls the multipliers, strong Dirichlet convergence controls the derivative terms, and the interpolants converge to the given functions at every point. Green-kernel symmetry [14, Remark 3.4.15] and the energy-integrability identity [14, Proposition 3.5.7 and its local variant, Proposition 3.5.10] identify the resulting pairings with integration of these bounded potentials against their Laplacians. Thus the measure in the statement is 12D[b2]−bD[b]\tfrac12D[b^2]-bD[b]21​D[b2]−bD[b], with the Borel product of the original representative, and not an independently chosen representative. The finite-skeleton rules give (eq:curve-product)–(eq:curve-chain); positivity and Cauchy–Schwarz pass through the same Dirichlet limit.

For the proper assertion, choose a lisse semipositive reference metric on the line after replacing it by a positive tensor power if necessary. More generally a fixed difference of such reference metrics suffices. Its curvature is a finite combination of atoms at nonrigid points. The gap of a bounded subharmonic metric from this reference is bounded. Its Green potential therefore has finite energy by [14, Proposition 3.5.7]. Polarization gives the symmetric Green pairing and (eq:proper-curve-energy), with the mass of each Chern measure equal to the degree of its line.

Finally, if EC(g)=0E_C(g)=0EC​(g)=0, Cauchy–Schwarz with the elementary Green function gx,yg_{x,y}gx,y​ gives g(x)=g(y)g(x)=g(y)g(x)=g(y) for all nonrigid x,yx,yx,y. In each local frame the subharmonic weights of rrr and of p+g(x)p+g(x)p+g(x) therefore agree at all such points. They agree everywhere by [14, Lemma 3.4.1]. Thus the gap is constant at every point. ◻

Proposition (The curve contact theorem). Let C/FC/FC/F be smooth projective geometrically integral, and LLL ample. Envelopes on a normal model

We prove continuity of the ample envelopes used in Theorem “Projective contact and regularization”. Weighted base ideals encode the semipositive minorants of a model obstacle. We replace them by test ideals to obtain global generation after one fixed ample twist. The required comparison comes from subadditivity with a vertical correction independent of the ideals and their exponents. Dividing logarithmic norms by degree makes the resulting error tend to zero.

Throughout this appendix RRR is a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic, F=Frac⁡(R)F=\operatorname{Frac}(R)F=Frac(R) has characteristic zero, π\piπ is a uniformizer, and λ=−log⁡∣π∣>0\lambda=-\log|\pi|>0λ=−log∣π∣>0. No finiteness or perfection assumption is imposed on the residue field. All test ideals are those of [1, Definition 8.37]; after completion we use the stable complete-local ideals of [1, Definition 8.13].

To globalize the correction, we need finitely many local differents whose sum is the unit ideal on the generic fiber. The next lemma obtains them from finite projections that are étale on a covering of that fiber. Their common failure is then supported vertically and is killed by one power of π\piπ.

Lemma (Finite projections and a vertical different). Let X\mathcal XX be normal, integral, projective and flat over RRR, with smooth generic fiber XXX of dimension nnn. There are finitely many finite morphisms fj:X→PRnf_j:\mathcal X\to\mathbb P_R^nfj​:X→PRn​ whose generic étale loci cover XXX. The sum J\mathfrak JJ of their coherent Noether-different ideals contains πC0OX\pi^{C_0}\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}πC0​OX​ for some C0C_0C0​.

Proof. Choose a relatively very ample line H\mathcal HH. On the special fiber, choose n+1n+1n+1 homogeneous parameters without a common zero. This works over an arbitrary residue field: at each stage, Serre interpolation provides a high-degree section nonzero at a chosen closed point of each component of the preceding zero locus. The dimension drops at each step. Taking powers makes the degrees equal; taking further powers permits lifting the sections to X\mathcal XX by Serre vanishing. Every tuple congruent to these lifts modulo π\piπ has no base point on X\mathcal XX: a nonempty proper closed base locus would meet the special fiber. It defines a finite morphism to PRn\mathbb P_R^nPRn​, because the pullback of O(1)\mathcal O(1)O(1) is relatively ample and so no fiber can have positive dimension.

Fix a closed point x∈Xx\in Xx∈X. Increase the degree until sections surject onto its first infinitesimal neighborhood. Since κ(x)/F\kappa(x)/Fκ(x)/F is separable, one can prescribe one nonzero section and nnn ratios with independent differentials at xxx. Being étale at xxx is therefore a nonempty Zariski-open condition on the tuple; the determinant condition can be expressed over FFF by its field norm. The congruence coset of lifts modulo π\piπ is Zariski dense in the FFF-vector space of tuples, since FFF is infinite and the section module is a full RRR-lattice. Choose a tuple in this open set. The resulting generic étale loci cover every closed point of XXX, hence all of the Jacobson scheme XXX. Quasi-compactness selects finitely many morphisms.

On affine target charts their Noether-different ideals glue, since the diagonal ideal is finitely generated and annihilators commute with localization. On the smooth generic fiber the different is a unit at every étale point; see [12, §49.12]. Thus J∣X=OX\mathfrak J|_X=\mathcal O_XJ∣X​=OX​. The coherent quotient OX/J\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}/\mathfrak JOX​/J is supported on the special fiber. A finite affine cover gives one exponent C0C_0C0​. ◻

Fix an effective integral vertical Weil divisor Δ0\Delta_0Δ0​ such that KX+Δ0K_{\mathcal X}+\Delta_0KX​+Δ0​ is Cartier. There is an integer C≥0C\geq0C≥0, independent of the nonzero coherent ideals a,b\mathfrak a,\mathfrak ba,b and rational exponents s,t≥0s,t\geq0s,t≥0, such that

πCτ(X,Δ0,asbt)⊂τ(X,Δ0,as)τ(X,Δ0,bt).\pi^C\tau(\mathcal X,\Delta_0,\mathfrak a^s\mathfrak b^t) \subset \tau(\mathcal X,\Delta_0,\mathfrak a^s) \tau(\mathcal X,\Delta_0,\mathfrak b^t).πCτ(X,Δ0​,asbt)⊂τ(X,Δ0​,as)τ(X,Δ0​,bt).

Proof. Choose TTT globally with πTOX⊂OX(−Δ0)\pi^T\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\subset\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}(-\Delta_0)πTOX​⊂OX​(−Δ0​). It exists because the latter coherent ideal is the unit ideal on XXX. It gives c=πTc=\pi^Tc=πT in every local canonical embedding above.

Fix a closed point yyy of the special fiber and a finite projection from Lemma “Finite projections and a vertical different”. Complete the regular local ring of PRn\mathbb P_R^nPRn​ at the image of yyy. Its finite algebra splits into complete local factors; the factor at yyy is S=O^X,yS=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{\mathcal X,y}S=OX,y​. It is a normal domain by excellence. Both rings have dimension n+1n+1n+1, so the map from the complete regular domain AAA to SSS is injective. An original Noether-different tensor witness base changes to the finite completed algebra and projects in both tensor factors to a witness for S/AS/AS/A. Thus the completed image of the global different is contained in NS/A\mathfrak N_{S/A}NS/A​.

Apply Proposition “Complete-local corrected subadditivity”. Corollary 8.40 of [1] identifies the completed global test ideals with the complete-local ones, and faithful flatness descends the containment. Sum over the finitely many projections and use πC0O⊂J\pi^{C_0}\mathcal O\subset\mathfrak JπC0​O⊂J. This gives (eq:global-correction) with C=T+C0C=T+C_0C=T+C0​ at every closed special-fiber point. A nonzero coherent failure quotient on the proper RRR-scheme would have such a point in its support. The containment therefore holds everywhere, with a constant chosen before the ideals and exponents. ◻

Remark. The uncorrected subadditivity in [1, Theorem 8.41(h)] applies on a regular scheme without a boundary in its two factors. In Theorem “Global fixed correction”, the scheme is normal and the boundary Δ0\Delta_0Δ0​ occurs in both factors. The factor πC\pi^CπC accounts for these differences. Its independence of the ideals and the exponents will give an error of order m−1m^{-1}m−1 in the envelope construction. Fang–Gubler–Künnemann prove continuity for model obstacles on regular models carrying an ample extension, and for arbitrary continuous obstacles under resolution of projective models [8, Theorem 1.1]. The proof below instead uses Theorem “Global fixed correction” on one normal model and retains a uniform error term throughout the construction.

Algebraic coordinates and a common local domain

The projective approximation theorem must be applied to local potentials without changing them near the test support. The collar in Lemma “A common collar for decreasing families” achieves this for an entire decreasing family at once: its first terms and limits determine a common bound, and that bound determines one barrier and one local domain. The last two lemmas transfer these constructions to the analytic spaces of Convention conv:spaces, including their integration normalizations.

In the first three lemmas, F∈GKF\in\mathcal G_KF∈GK​, π\piπ is the chosen uniformizer, and λ=−log⁡∣π∣\lambda=-\log|\pi|λ=−log∣π∣. All constructions take place over FFF on the indicated ordinary neighborhoods.

Lemma (One inactive floor). In Lemma “A common collar for decreasing families”, suppose that Pi,j,m↓Ri,jP_{i,j,m}\downarrow R_{i,j}Pi,j,m​↓Ri,j​ are pure Fubini–Study metrics on LLL. Their weights on the same VVV, and all their nonnegative translates in λQ\lambda\mathbb QλQ, have finite tropically convex rational PL presentations in algebraic coordinates. The algebraic chart and VVV are independent of i,j,mi,j,mi,j,m.

Proof. After clearing a tensor denominator, each weight in the fixed frame has the form P=1Nmax⁡alog⁡∣sa/e⊗N∣,P=\frac1N\max_a\log|s_a/e^{\otimes N}|,P=N1​amax​log∣sa​/e⊗N∣, where the finitely many sas_asa​ generate NLNLNL. Rational constants in λQ\lambda\mathbb QλQ can be absorbed by raising to one common tensor power and multiplying sections by powers of π\piπ. All these weights lie above their limits as m→∞m\to\inftym→∞, and those limits lie above the finitely many bounded functions ui+cu_i+cui​+c on VVV. Choose a single B∈λQB\in\lambda\mathbb QB∈λQ strictly below all of them. This floor will keep the tropical expression finite at zeros of individual sections, while remaining inactive in every approximating weight. Then P=max⁡{B,P}P=\max\{B,P\}P=max{B,P} on VVV, for every i,j,mi,j,mi,j,m.

Write B=aλ/N0=(1/N0)log⁡∣π−a∣B=a\lambda/N_0=(1/N_0)\log|\pi^{-a}|B=aλ/N0​=(1/N0​)log∣π−a∣. Appending the nonzero constant regular function π−a\pi^{-a}π−a to the algebraic moment coordinates represents the floor by a rational linear expression with zero constant term. In the valuation coordinates tf=−log⁡∣f∣t_f=-\log|f|tf​=−log∣f∣, the resulting function is a maximum of rational linear functions −tf/N-t_f/N−tf​/N. The floor remains finite even when some section coordinates vanish. Near such a point, those coordinates have value +∞+\infty+∞ and their branches are inactive; deleting them leaves a finite rational PL expression on a neighborhood of that point. Restrict the ambient extended tropical domain to the locus where the appended constant coordinate is finite. The finitely many possible subsets of inactive coordinates give the finite PL cover in Wu’s definition. The expression is continuous on this domain and convex on its finite-coordinate part, hence tropically convex by [16, Lemma 3.4(1), Definitions 3.1 and 3.7]. The appended constant coordinate is algebraic; if an affine embedding is desired, include generators of the fixed affine coordinate ring as additional coordinates which the displayed function ignores.

A nonnegative translate still lies above BBB, and a translate in λQ\lambda\mathbb QλQ is handled by the same section-power operation. Thus the floor and the underlying domain are independent of the indices and of the translate. Subtracting the fixed ccc in (eq:common-collar-weights) only replaces the floor by B−cB-cB−c. This construction does not require setting λ=1\lambda=1λ=1. ◻

Lemma (Ordinary algebraic neighborhoods). Let XXX be good, Hausdorff, boundaryless and quasi-smooth over KKK. For every x∈Xx\in Xx∈X and ordinary neighborhood NNN of xxx, there is a smaller ordinary neighborhood W⊂NW\subset NW⊂N which is KKK-analytically isomorphic to an ordinary open of a smooth affine KKK-variety.

Proof. Shrink NNN inside the interior of an affinoid neighborhood of xxx; it is then separated and remains boundaryless. Ducros’s algebraization lemma [7, Lemma (0.21)], applied with the full group of positive radii, gives an affinoid neighborhood VVV of xxx in NNN, identified with an affinoid domain in the analytification of a smooth affine KKK-variety YYY. No extension of KKK is made.

The relative-interior composition formula, with locally separated intermediate spaces [10, §2.11(3)–(4)], gives Int⁡(V/N)=Int⁡(V/K)=Int⁡(V/Yan),\operatorname{Int}(V/N)=\operatorname{Int}(V/K) =\operatorname{Int}(V/Y^{\mathrm{an}}),Int(V/N)=Int(V/K)=Int(V/Yan), because NNN and YanY^{\mathrm{an}}Yan are boundaryless. Relative interiors of analytic-domain embeddings are their ordinary topological interiors; see [13, Fact 3.4.11 and Fact 4.2.15(i)]. The common interior is therefore ordinary open in both NNN and YanY^{\mathrm{an}}Yan, and contains xxx since VVV was a neighborhood. It is the required WWW. One may shrink it further to have compact closure in a larger such chart. ◻

Lemma (Finite constants and integration). Let YYY be a smooth integral affine KKK-variety, and let LLL be the algebraic closure of KKK in K(Y)K(Y)K(Y). Then L/KL/KL/K is finite separable, YYY is naturally an LLL-variety, and Y/LY/LY/L is smooth and geometrically integral. Viewing this same analytic space over KKK or over LLL does not change its functions, absolute values or classical psh functions. If d=[L:K]d=[L:K]d=[L:K], the calibrated integration currents satisfy

[1]K=d[1]L.[1]_K=d[1]_L.[1]K​=d[1]L​.

Consequently the mixed currents and weighted currents, whenever constructed by the recursion in the main theorem, satisfy Tk,K=dTk,L,Sk,K=dSk,L.T_{k,K}=dT_{k,L},\qquad S_{k,K}=dS_{k,L}.Tk,K​=dTk,L​,Sk,K​=dSk,L​.

Proof. The extension L/KL/KL/K is finite because K(Y)/KK(Y)/KK(Y)/K is finitely generated, and it is separable in characteristic zero. Every element of LLL is integral over KKK, hence over the normal affine coordinate ring of YYY; it therefore belongs to that ring. This gives the LLL-structure. The diagonal factor of Y×KLY\times_K LY×K​L, singled out by L⊗KL→LL\otimes_K L\to LL⊗K​L→L, is YYY itself as an LLL-scheme. It is open and closed, so it is smooth over LLL. The function-field extension K(Y)/LK(Y)/LK(Y)/L is regular, giving geometric integrality.

There is a unique extension of the absolute value of the complete field KKK to LLL. Thus the two analytifications have the same points, topology and analytic functions. An E/LE/LE/L-curve test maps to the diagonal open-and-closed factor YL×LEY_L\times_L EYL​×L​E of YK×KEY_K\times_K EYK​×K​E, and is therefore a permitted KKK-curve test. Conversely, for an E/KE/KE/K-curve test, pass to a completed algebraic closure Ω/E\Omega/EΩ/E. Then L⊗KΩ=∏σ:L→ΩΩL\otimes_K\Omega=\prod_{\sigma:L\to\Omega}\OmegaL⊗K​Ω=∏σ:L→Ω​Ω. The inverse images of these factors are open-and-closed curves. Classicality over LLL gives subharmonicity on each of them. Sheafiness and descent under analytic field extension [10, Proposition 3.5(7)] give subharmonicity on the original EEE-curve. Upper semicontinuity and local boundedness are unchanged.

The moment skeletons are the same in the two interpretations. Forgetting LLL multiplies each finite moment degree by ddd; its calibration is therefore multiplied by ddd, as in [6, Remark 14.4.3]. This proves (eq:finite-constant-calibration). Differentiation and multiplication by a fixed Borel function are linear. Induction through the recursive definition gives the same single factor ddd at every exterior degree, not dkd^kdk. ◻
